description: Power, device-reported energy, electrical readings and exporter diagnostics for pyprom-exporters. Portable Prometheus data source and regex-safe fleet filters; no external plugins.

options.content: **Power in W · energy in Wh · exporter health.** Filter devices above. Compact legends below each graph identify devices; hover a line for its label and value. The dashed line is total power. Colours can repeat.

panels.title: Read the fleet at a glance

panels.description: Prometheus scrape health across selected exporters. A successful scrape does not prove that every plug refreshed. No targets means the job or exporter selection has no matching target.
panels.title: Exporter

panels.description: Count of selected device power series in the latest successful scrape. This is not an online count; unsupported, missing and failed readings are omitted. Repeated monitoring of one physical plug by different exporters counts more than once.
panels.title: Reporting plugs

panels.description: Sum of available selected device power readings in watts. Missing devices are not estimated; this can be a partial fleet total.
panels.title: Power now

panels.description: Sum of available device-reported energy today, in Wh. Resets at each plug’s local midnight, not the browser timezone. Not energy over the selected dashboard range.
panels.title: Energy today

panels.description: Sum of available device-reported energy this calendar month, in Wh. Resets at each plug’s month boundary. Not a lifetime counter or energy over the selected dashboard range.
panels.title: Energy month

panels.description: Seconds since the most recent Prometheus scrape attempt, successful or failed. This is not the age of the device reading: a timed-out live refresh can return an older snapshot. See SDK update timing for collection status; it does not establish physical sensor freshness.
panels.title: Scrape age

panels.description: Instantaneous watts per device and the sum of available readings. Gaps remain visible; a zero reading is a real reported zero. Host addresses distinguish repeated aliases. Device colors follow their legend names across panels. The dashed amber line is the selected total.
panels.title: Power over time

panels.description: Up to ten selected devices with the highest current reported wattage. Rankings omit unavailable readings. Each row names its device, host and exporter; colors match the history panels even when ranking changes.
panels.title: Largest loads now · top 10

panels.description: Device-reported gauge in Wh, shown without rate or increase. It resets at midnight in the plug’s timezone. Missing samples remain gaps; a reset is expected. Unsupported devices have no series.
panels.title: Energy accumulated today

panels.description: Device-reported gauge in Wh, shown without rate or increase. It resets at the month boundary in the plug’s timezone. Missing samples remain gaps; a reset is expected. Unsupported devices have no series.
panels.title: Energy accumulated this month

panels.description: Available device readings only. Hardware and firmware capabilities vary; no data does not mean a zero reading. No universal alarm threshold is imposed because regional supply and plug ratings differ.
panels.title: Voltage

panels.description: Available device readings only. Hardware and firmware capabilities vary; no data does not mean a zero reading. No universal alarm threshold is imposed because regional supply and plug ratings differ.
panels.title: Current

panels.description: Reported received signal strength in dBm. Values closer to zero indicate stronger reception. Not a connectivity or packet-loss measurement.
panels.title: Wi-Fi signal over time

panels.description: Current Wi-Fi signal in dBm, weakest first. Values closer to 0 indicate stronger received signal. Colors identify devices and match their history traces; they do not classify signal quality. Rows include device alias, host and exporter so identical aliases remain distinguishable. Missing readings remain absent; scrape success does not establish device-reading freshness.
panels.title: Wi-Fi signal now
Device updates · SDK outcomes and timing

panels.description: Duration of the latest completed SDK update attempt in seconds, including python-kasa retries. Excludes queueing, discovery and disconnect work. Zero means no completed attempt yet. A failed attempt can have a duration; it does not mean the reading is fresh.
panels.title: Update duration

panels.description: Latest SDK update outcome: 1 succeeded, 0 failed or no successful update has occurred. Configured hosts that have never been discovered appear as unknown. This is not relay state or proof of physical sensor freshness.
panels.title: Latest update outcome

panels.description: Seconds since the last successful SDK update. This is not physical sensor freshness: a device can return cached measurements. No data means no successful update timestamp is available, including hosts that have never updated. Interpret the age against your polling interval and update timeout.
panels.title: Time since successful update

panels.description: Rate of failed SDK update attempts, including timeouts. Counters persist through rediscovery and reset when the exporter process restarts. At least two samples are required; a missing series is not zero.
panels.title: Failed updates per second

panels.description: Rate of SDK update attempts that timed out. These attempts also contribute to failed updates. Includes expiry of the configured update timeout; does not count discovery failures or Prometheus HTTP scrape failures. At least two samples are required.
panels.title: Update timeouts per second
Exporter health · all hosts on selected exporters

panels.description: All discovered devices retained by the selected exporters. Host/device filters do not apply. This may include unsupported or failed devices and is not an online count.
panels.title: Inventory

panels.description: Samples from the latest scrape across selected exporters, including process metrics. Host/device filters do not apply. A failed scrape may report zero.
panels.title: Samples

panels.description: Latest longest scrape duration among selected exporters. Live probing contributes to this duration. Compare with the configured Prometheus scrape timeout; this stack defaults to 25 seconds.
panels.title: Longest scrape

panels.description: Total resident memory reported by the selected exporter processes. Optional process metrics may be absent on unsupported platforms.
panels.title: Memory

panels.description: CPU seconds per wall-clock second across selected exporters; 1 means one fully busy core. This is a counter rate, independent of the plug energy gauges. At least two process samples are required.
panels.title: CPU · cores

panels.description: Prometheus targets matching the job/exporter filters, whether their latest scrape succeeded or failed. Host/device filters do not apply.
panels.title: Targets

panels.description: Duration of each HTTP scrape attempt, including the wait for live updates and serialization. Healthy readings can finish before failed-device recovery. Compare with the configured exporter wait and Prometheus timeout; investigate repeated wait timeouts and update failures.
panels.title: Scrape duration over time

panels.description: 1 means Prometheus fetched and parsed an exporter response; 0 means the scrape failed. This is exporter reachability, not individual plug freshness or relay state.
panels.title: Scrape success over time

panels.description: Duration of the latest completed full refresh pass, including failed-device recovery work. Healthy readings can be published before this pass completes. Host and device filters do not apply.
panels.title: Refresh duration

panels.description: 1 while a device refresh pass is running, 0 when idle. Scrape sampling may miss short refreshes. Healthy readings can already be available while recovery continues. Host and device filters do not apply.
panels.title: Refresh in progress

panels.description: Rate of exporter callers that exhausted their wait for fresh updates and received the current snapshot. A successful HTTP scrape may still increment this counter. This is distinct from device timeouts; background polling normally serves the cache without waiting. Host and device filters do not apply.
panels.title: Scrape waits timed out per second

options.content:
**Start with exporter scrape status.** If it fails, check the Prometheus target and exporter logs. If it succeeds but plug data is missing, check configured hosts, LAN reachability, credentials and device capabilities.

**A successful scrape can contain an older snapshot.** Update outcome, duration and time since the last successful SDK update help explain stalled readings; SDK success does not prove physical sensor freshness. Failed updates are omitted when their result is available, and healthy readings can publish while recovery continues. Check exporter logs for details. The operational panels require pyprom-exporters 0.3.0 or later; older exporters show No data.

**Energy is device-reported Wh.** Today/month gauges reset on the plug’s calendar. They are not counters and are not converted into hourly/yearly estimates. Historical `kasa_*` data is not combined with these different metrics.
